sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Sunil Kumar Yadav - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri Viraj Godha - Pl for the respondent/State.
ORDER Heard with the aid of case diary.

This is first application filed under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (in short "B.N.S.S."), for grant of bail to the applicant/accused, relating to FIR/Crime No.47/2024 dated (not mentioned) registered at Police Station - Juni, District Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 363, 366 and 376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 5L/6 of POCSO Act.
2.
Prosecution story, in brief is that at the time of the incident, the prosecutrix was minor aged below 18 years.
Prior to the incident, there was conversation between the applicant and prosecutrix through Instagram App and mobile phone.

The applicant gave false pretext to marry her and on 05.02.2024, after the call of the applicant, the prosecutrix met him at Sheetal NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23330 2 MCRC-30678-2024 Hotel, Indore.
Thereafter, both of them went to Vijaywada and other places.
The applicant kept the prosecutrix for around 02 months.

Meanwhile,
he committed rape upon her repeatedly.
Prosecutrix was recovered on 06.04.2024.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused submits that the applicant has not committed the offence and he has falsely been implicated in the case.

It is submitted that prosecutrix is an illiterate Chandresh @ Chandu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152303427/
1 lady and as per radiology report, at the time of the incident, she was aged around 17-19 years,
therefore it cannot be said that at the time of the incident, she was below 15 years of age.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also submitted that the prosecutrix was a major lady more than 18 years of age.
She voluntarily left her house and went alongwith the applicant.
She was consenting party for sexual intercourse.
He is in custody since 05.02.2024.
Investigation is completed and charge sheet has been filed.
Conclusion of trial will take considerable long time for its disposal, therefore, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the non-applicant/State has opposed the prayer and prayed for its rejection.

5. Having considered the rival submissions and after perusal of the case diary so also considering the facts and circumstances of the case, without commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is of the view that applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail hence, the application is allowed.

6. It is directed that the applicant - CHANDRESH @ CHANDU shall be released on bail upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:23330 3 MCRC-30678-2024 Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerning Trial Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this behalf by the Trial Court during pendency of the trial.

It is further directed that applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of trial but in case of bail jump, it shall become ineffective.
8. With the aforesaid, this application is allowed and stands disposed of.
Certified copy, as per Rules.

(PRAKASH CHANDRA GUPTA) JUDGE Shruti Chandresh @ Chandu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152303427/
